messages:

Subject: Order Form indemnity — proposed allocation and notice procedure

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are HelixMed's proposed redlines to the MSA + Order Form focusing on the indemnity sections (third-party IP infringement + customer-driven claims). High-level items we care about:

- Clear defense allocation for third-party IP claims (we're pushing for HelixMed to control defense for claims arising from our integration of the product).
- Evidence custody and proof-of-claim timelines — we need a concrete handoff path to gather technical artifacts quickly.
- Insurance offsets (we prefer carrier-first recovery before invoicing Redwood).
- Cap / carveouts related to customer-provided data and fine-tuning.

Please see the attached HelixMed_MSARedlines_20251005.docx for tracked changes. Procurement would like a response by EOD Wednesday so we can review with counsel. If it helps, we can do a 30-minute call Thursday AM to work through the disputed paragraphs.

Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed allocation and notice procedure

Erin — thanks for sending and for the thoughtful redlines. Mateo here from Redwood, looping in our legal and sales leads to accelerate. Quick reactions and next steps below.

Summary of Redwood positions (high-level):
- We can accept a defend-and-indemnify approach for third-party IP claims that are directly caused by Redwood's model outputs or code defects, but we need to preserve the right to control defense where appropriate (standard carve: Redwood can assume defense with customer consent; otherwise we request notice + cooperation).
- For customer data / customer-supplied prompts or fine-tuning, we propose a narrow carveout (Redwood not responsible for claims arising solely from customer-provided content).
- Insurance offset: acceptable in principle — we'd propose ordering of remedies: insurance proceeds first, then indemnity subject to any deductible. We do not want full subrogation waivers that eliminate Redwood's recourse.
- Evidence custody / technical handoff: Operations needs explicit SLAs (who will snapshot KV cache, session logs, and model input traces). Kimberley/legal — can you propose a short list of artifacts we can commit to provide?

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to push a tracked redline with limited language on defense control and settlement approval thresholds.
2) We agree a 30-day notification window from HelixMed for alleged claims to avoid surprise, but open to discuss 60-day cure if HelixMed needs it.
3) Quick call Thursday 10/09 10:00am PT to walk legal redlines.

Attaching a short redline summary to make the choices concrete.

Thanks — Mateo
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed allocation and notice procedure

Hi Erin / Mateo — Kimberly from Redwood Legal. Thanks for the redlines, Erin — I reviewed the doc and drafted focused alternatives that (a) keep HelixMed protected for customer-caused incidents and (b) limit Redwood's exposure to our operational control and model defects.

Key legal edits I propose (see attached track changes):
1) Defense control: Redwood would reserve the right to assume defense of any third-party IP claim where Redwood's products or service (including the model weights and serving runtime) are alleged to be the primary cause. If Redwood assumes defense, HelixMed would have the right to participate at its own cost. If HelixMed wants to control defense, we request (i) prior notice, and (ii) Redwood's written consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

2) Settlement approval: Any settlement that admits liability or imposes obligations on Redwood must be subject to Redwood's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). For monetary settlements paid by Redwood, we propose a $250k settlement approval threshold requiring exec-level signoff.

3) Insurance offsets & subrogation: We agree that insurance proceeds should be credited first. Redwood will not waive subrogation unless in limited, reciprocal circumstances. We propose explicit language to preserve payment flow for the insured party's carrier recovery.

4) Evidence custody & logs: Operationally, Redwood can provide exported request traces, model input/response hashes, and KV-cache snapshots for the period identified in the notice, subject to privacy/data-minimization. We propose the following handoff workflow: (a) HelixMed issues notice and evidence request; (b) Redwood preserves relevant logs and creates a technical evidence bundle within 10 business days; (c) parties agree on secure transfer link. If HelixMed requires full raw prompt logs, we need a DPA amendment and scope-limited retention.

5) Carveouts: Redwood requests a carveout for claims arising solely from HelixMed's use of customer-supplied training material, including any fine-tuning HelixMed performs. We propose a representative definition for "Customer-Provided Content" to be added to the Order Form.

6) Cap/limitation structure: For indemnity arising from IP infringement that is not otherwise covered by insurance, Redwood proposes a cap equal to the greater of (i) the fees paid for the affected Order Form in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000. We are open to negotiation on the numbers.

If HelixMed is comfortable with these principles, we'll issue a clean tracked redline that resolves the disputed paras and include the operational evidence checklist as an appendix. I also included a short paragraph about the notice/cure window — my preference is 30 days notice + 30 days cure; if HelixMed requires 60 days, we can discuss, but we want an enforceable timeline.

Please confirm whether HelixMed wants Redwood to assume defense in the scenarios above or to leave defense entirely to the customer. If you prefer defense control, we will need clearer settlement guardrails.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachment: legal_redlines_trackchanges_20251007.docx

Date: 2025-10-08T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed allocation and notice procedure

Kimberly and team — thanks for the thoughtful reply. I reviewed your edits with our GC and procurement. A few quick responses:

- Defense control: HelixMed's preference remains to control defense for claims that directly relate to our integration or customer-facing configurations, but we are willing to agree to a joint-control model for matters clearly caused by Redwood's runtime or model (as Kimberley described). We'll accept Redwood assuming defense in those narrowly-defined cases, subject to your settlement guardrails.

- Notice/cure window: Procurement is asking for a 60-day cure window (instead of 30) because we need time to triage across our legal and clinical teams. Would Redwood accept 60 days in exchange for a slightly higher settlement approval threshold?

- Evidence custody: We appreciate Redwood's operational proposal. Two asks: (1) HelixMed requests that any evidence bundle be delivered via our secure egress link within 10 business days of notice; (2) if Redwood needs a DPA amendment to provide raw prompts, our security team will review separately, but we'd prefer to avoid expanding retention if possible.

- Cap: HelixMed cannot accept the $1,000,000 floor as a hard cap. We propose either a mutual cap tied to a multiple of the Order Form fees or an uncapped indemnity for willful infringement.

Next steps:
1) Procurement will review Kimberly's track-changes and propose a compromise number for cap/threshold (we will aim to propose by Monday 10/13).
2) Contracts team will circulate an updated Order Form with the agreed defense/settlement language and a DocuSign envelope when we have numbers.

Thanks — Erin
Erin Frost
Director, Strategic Sourcing | HelixMed
